newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares end firm in thin turnover.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares end firm in thin turnover.

text.p: Chilean blue chips resumed their winning run to close sharply higher in thin trade on Monday with the market boosted by foreign demand for stocks including telecom Telex, said traders.
The bolsa is expected to open a notch higher with turnover likely to be stronger, they said.
The 40-share .IPSA index closed up 1.13 percent at 111.79 points. The general .IGPA index gained 0.64 percent to 5,260.96 points.
Volume shrank from 13 billion pesos Friday to 7.7 billion pesos.
Local turnover was dominated by brokers trading their own portfolios, said dealers.
But the IPSA index was driven higher by buy orders in New York for Chilean-issued American Depositary Receipts including Telex, Endesa and Enersis, they said.
Telex climbed on news the company and rival carrier CTC have agreed to call an end to their long-running legal spats, said one trader.
Other winners included Cochrane which resumed its upward march on news announced last week that the company has won a large contract in Brazil, said dealers.
Losers included winery Conche y Toro VCO.Nu, down 2.22 percent at 220 pesos, steel-maker Cap, down 0.8 percent at 1,240 pesos and paper producer CMPC which lost 0.24 percent at 4,669 pesos.
